blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — lamotrigine serious-rash warning and client teaching
stem: A client who recently started lamotrigine develops a new rash. Which instruction should the nurse give?

options.A: Continue lamotrigine at the current dose and monitor the rash at home unless blistering, mucosal lesions, or fever later develops.
options.B: Skip the next scheduled dose, then restart lamotrigine at the same dose if the rash becomes less noticeable without other symptoms.
options.C: Continue lamotrigine but slow any future dose increases because a reduced titration rate is sufficient once a rash has appeared.
options.D: Stop taking lamotrigine and promptly contact the prescriber for evaluation unless the rash is clearly established as unrelated to the drug.

rationale: Current lamotrigine labeling carries a boxed warning for life-threatening serious skin rashes, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Because benign and serious rashes cannot reliably be distinguished at onset, the label states that lamotrigine should be discontinued at the first sign of rash unless the rash is clearly not drug related. It also states not to restart lamotrigine after discontinuation for rash unless potential benefits clearly outweigh the risks. Therefore D is the safest instruction. A and C continue exposure despite the warning, and B proposes an unsupervised restart that is not label-supported.
educational_objective: Teach clients taking lamotrigine to discontinue it and promptly seek prescriber evaluation when a new rash appears unless the rash is clearly unrelated to the drug, because benign and life-threatening rashes cannot be reliably distinguished at onset.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: DailyMed updated July 30, 2026; version 16 current, published August 3, 2026; boxed warning and serious-rash content updated October 2025; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Boxed Warning — Serious Skin Rashes; Warnings and Precautions §5.1 Serious Skin Rashes; Dosage and Administration §2.1 — do not restart after discontinuation for rash unless benefits clearly outweigh risks.
source_claim_supported: Lamotrigine can cause life-threatening serious rashes; benign and serious rashes cannot reliably be distinguished at onset, so lamotrigine should be discontinued at the first sign of rash unless clearly not drug related; restart after rash-related discontinuation requires careful benefit-risk consideration.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: educate client about medications; recognize and evaluate adverse effects; intervene for adverse medication effects.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as plausible rash-management instructions without the original absolute-word distractor cue.
Length-balanced the options while preserving the exact label-based discontinuation exception for a rash clearly unrelated to lamotrigine.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms D uniquely follows the current boxed warning and does not overstate the rule because it retains the label's exception for a rash clearly not drug related. A–C represent plausible but unsafe continuation or unsupervised restart strategies.
